{"actor_id":"EO:13764","char_end":51715,"char_start":47207,"confidence":"medium","effective_class":"unknown","effective_date":null,"effective_wording":[{"char_end":10411,"char_start":9734,"text":"(a) Executive branch vetting policies and procedures relating to suitability, contractor or Federal employee fitness, eligibility to hold a sensitive position, authorization to be issued a Federal credential for access to federally controlled facilities and information systems, and eligibility for access to classified information shall be aligned using consistent standards to the extent possible, shall provide for reciprocal recognition, and shall ensure cost-effective, timely, and efficient protection of the national interest, while providing fair treatment to those upon whom the Federal Government relies to conduct our Nation's business and protect national security."},{"char_end":11078,"char_start":10851,"text":"To help fulfill these responsibilities, there shall be a primary executive branch investigative service provider whose mission is to provide effective, efficient, and secure background investigations for the Federal Government."},{"char_end":20113,"char_start":19711,"text":"\"(n) 'National Background Investigations Bureau' (NBIB) means the National Background Investigations Bureau, established within the Office of Personnel Management under section 1103(a)(3) of title 5, United States Code, or a successor entity, with responsibility for conducting effective, efficient, and secure personnel background investigations pursuant to law, rule, regulation, or Executive Order.\""},{"char_end":22855,"char_start":22190,"text":"\"(b) The aligned executive branch-wide vetting enterprise shall employ modern and consistent standards and methods, enable innovations with enterprise information technology capabilities and end-to-end automation to the extent practicable, and ensure that relevant information maintained by agencies can be accessed and shared rapidly across the executive branch, while protecting national security, protecting privacy-related information, protecting civil rights and civil liberties, ensuring resulting decisions are in the national interest and in accordance with due process requirements, and providing the Federal Government with an effective trusted workforce."},{"char_end":32056,"char_start":31684,"text":"\"(vii) shall, pursuant to section 1104 of title 5, United States Code, prescribe performance standards and a system of oversight for any suitability or fitness function delegated by the Director to the head of another agency, including uniform and consistent policies and procedures to ensure the effective, efficient, timely, and secure completion of delegated functions."},{"char_end":33500,"char_start":33264,"text":"\"(vi) shall be responsible for developing uniform and consistent policies and procedures to ensure the effective, efficient, timely, and secure completion of investigations and adjudications relating to eligibility for a PIV credential;"},{"char_end":37041,"char_start":36701,"text":"\"(iii) shall be responsible for developing and issuing uniform and consistent policies and procedures to ensure the effective, efficient, timely, and secure completion of investigations, polygraphs, and adjudications relating to determinations of eligibility for access to classified information or eligibility to hold a sensitive position;"},{"char_end":40365,"char_start":40256,"text":"\"(2) provide effective, efficient, and secure personnel background investigations for the Federal Government;"},{"char_end":42890,"char_start":42694,"text":"\"(c) Delegations and designations of investigative authority in place on the date of establishment of the National Background Investigations Bureau shall remain in effect until amended or revoked."},{"char_end":44394,"char_start":43956,"text":"\"(ii) establish and maintain within as applicable, meets standards for eligibility for access to classified information or to hold a sensitive position, suitability, fitness, or credentialing, established by the respective Executive Agent;"},{"char_end":51057,"char_start":50743,"text":"\"(f) Existing delegations of authority made pursuant to Executive Order 13381 of June 27, 2005, as amended, to any agency relating to granting eligibility for access to classified information shall remain in effect, subject to the exercise of authorities pursuant to this order to revise or revoke such delegation."},{"char_end":51290,"char_start":51059,"text":"\"(g) Existing delegations of authority made by the Office of Personnel Management to any agency relating to suitability or fitness shall \n(C) Executive Order 12333 or any applicable agency procedures pursuant \nto Executive Order 12333; \n(D) this order or any applicable agency policies and procedures issued \nor updated pursuant to this order (or the policies and procedures identified \nin section 2(c)(iv)(A) of this order before they are updated pursuant to \nsection 2(c)(iv)(B) of this order); \n(E) any successor statute, order, policies, or procedures to those identified \nin section 4(d)(iii)(B)–(D) of this order; or \n(F) any other statute, order, policies, or procedures adopted after the \ndate of this order that provides privacy and civil liberties safeguards \nwith respect to United States signals intelligence activities within the \nscope of this order, as identified in a list published and updated by \nthe Attorney General, in consultation with the Director of National Intel-\nligence."},{"char_end":53477,"char_start":51870,"text":"(k) ‘‘Qualifying complaint’’ means a complaint, submitted in writing, that: \n(i) alleges a covered violation has occurred that pertains to personal infor-\nmation of or about the complainant, a natural person, reasonably believed \nto have been transferred to the United States from a qualifying state \nafter the effective date of the Attorney General’s designation for such \nstate, as provided in section 3(f)(i) of this order; \n(ii) includes the following basic information to enable a review: information \nthat forms the basis for alleging that a covered violation has occurred, \nwhich need not demonstrate that the complainant’s data has in fact been \nsubject to United States signals intelligence activities; the nature of the \nrelief sought; the specific means by which personal information of or \nabout the complainant was believed to have been transmitted to the United \nStates; the identities of the United States Government entities believed \nto be involved in the alleged violation (if known); and any other measures \nthe complainant pursued to obtain the relief requested and the response \nreceived through those other measures; \n(iii) is not frivolous, vexatious, or made in bad faith; \n(iv) is brought on behalf of the complainant, acting on that person’s \nown behalf, and not as a representative of a governmental, nongovern-\nmental, or intergovernmental organization; and \n(v) is transmitted by the appropriate public authority in a qualifying \nstate, after it has verified the identity of the complainant and that the \ncomplaint satisfies the conditions of section 5(k)(i)–(iv) of this order."}],"exceptions_text":[],"filing_date":null,"id":"ACT:EO:12333>EO:14086","names_target":true,"notes":"Machine lead only; - **ACT:EO:12333>EO:14086@79a7708d9301bb65**; S25de9667102755fc6969fa08; {"actor_id":"EO:14086","char_end":50179,"char_start":48440,"confidence":"medium","effective_class":"on_signing","effective_date":"2022-10-07","effective_wording":[{"char_end":8325,"char_start":8016,"text":"(A) Under section 102A of the National Security Act of 1947, as amended \n(50 U.S.C. 3024), the Director must establish priorities for the Intelligence \nCommunity to ensure the timely and effective collection of national intel-\nligence, including national intelligence collected through signals intel-\nligence."},{"char_end":45619,"char_start":43932,"text":"(i) To implement the redress mechanism established by section 3 of this \norder, the Attorney General is authorized to designate a country or regional \neconomic integration organization as a qualifying state for purposes of \nthe redress mechanism established pursuant to section 3 of this order, \neffective immediately or on a date specified by the Attorney General, \nif the Attorney General determines, in consultation with the Secretary \nof State, the Secretary of Commerce, and the Director, that: \n(A) the laws of the country, the regional economic integration organiza-\ntion, or the regional economic integration organization’s member countries \nrequire appropriate safeguards in the conduct of signals intelligence activi-\nties for United States persons’ personal information that is transferred \nfrom the United States to the territory of the country or a member country \nof the regional economic integration organization; \nVerDate Sep<11>2014 16:13 Oct 13, 2022 Jkt 259001 PO 00000 Frm 00011 Fmt 4705 Sfmt 4790 E:\\FR\\FM\\14OCE0.SGM 14OCE0jspears on DSK121TN23PROD with PREZ DOCS 3\n=== PDF page 12 of 15 ===\n62294 Federal Register / Vol. 87, No. 198 / Friday, October 14, 2022 / Presidential Documents \n(B) the country, the regional economic integration organization, or the \nregional economic integration organization’s member countries of the re-\ngional economic integration organization permit, or are anticipated to per-\nmit, the transfer of personal information for commercial purposes between \nthe territory of that country or those member countries and the territory \nof the United States; and \n(C) such designation would advance the national interests of the United \nStates."},{"char_end":46717,"char_start":45621,"text":"(ii) The Attorney General may revoke or amend such a designation, effective \nimmediately or on a date specified by the Attorney General, if the Attorney \nGeneral determines, in consultation with the Secretary of State, the Sec-\nretary of Commerce, and the Director, that: \n(A) the country, the regional economic integration organization, or the \nregional economic integration organization’s member countries do not pro-\nvide appropriate safeguards in the conduct of signals intelligence activities \nfor United States persons’ personal information that is transferred from \nthe United States to the territory of the country or to a member country \nof the regional economic integration organization; \n(B) the country, the regional economic integration organization, or the \nregional economic integration organization’s member countries do not per-\nmit the transfer of personal information for commercial purposes between \nthe territory of that country or those member countries and the territory \nof the United States; or \n(C) such designation is not in the national interests of the United States."},{"char_end":50179,"char_start":48440,"text":"(d) ‘‘Covered violation’’ means a violation that: \n(i) arises from signals intelligence activities conducted after the date of \nthis order regarding data transferred to the United States from a qualifying \nstate after the effective date of the Attorney General’s designation for \nsuch state, as provided in section 3(f)(i) of this order; \n(ii) adversely affects the complainant’s individual privacy and civil liberties \ninterests; and \n(iii) violates one or more of the following: \n(A) the United States Constitution; \nVerDate Sep<11>2014 16:13 Oct 13, 2022 Jkt 259001 PO 00000 Frm 00012 Fmt 4705 Sfmt 4790 E:\\FR\\FM\\14OCE0.SGM 14OCE0jspears on DSK121TN23PROD with PREZ DOCS 3\n=== PDF page 13 of 15 ===\n62295 Federal Register / Vol. 87, No. 198 / Friday, October 14, 2022 / Presidential Documents \n(B) the applicable sections of FISA or any applicable FISC-approved \nprocedures; the nature of the \nrelief sought; the specific means by which personal information of or \nabout the complainant was believed to have been transmitted to the United \nStates; the identities of the United States Government entities believed \nto be involved in the alleged violation (if known); and any other measures \nthe complainant pursued to obtain the relief requested and the response \nreceived through those other measures; \n(iii) is not frivolous, vexatious, or made in bad faith; \n(iv) is brought on behalf of the complainant, acting on that person’s \nown behalf, and not as a representative of a governmental, nongovern-\nmental, or intergovernmental organization; chronology does not decide legal effect.","provision_text":"Executive Order 12333 \nof December 4, 1981, as amended, is further amended as follows: \n(a) Subsection 1.5(a) is amended to read:\n‘‘(a)(1) Act as the principal adviser to the President for intelligence \nmatters related to the national security;\n‘‘(2) Act as the principal adviser to the National Security Council \nand Homeland Security Council for intelligence matters related to the \nnational security; and \n(b) Subsection 1.5(b) is amended to read:\n‘‘(b)(1) Develop such objectives and guidance for the Intelligence Commu-\nnity necessary, in the Director’s judgment, to ensure timely and effective \ncollection, processing, analysis, and dissemination of intelligence, of what-\never nature and from whatever source derived, concerning current and \npotential threats to the security of the United States and its interests, \nand to ensure that the National Foreign Intelligence Program (NFIP) is \nstructured adequately to achieve these requirements; and\n‘‘(2) Working with the Intelligence Community, ensure that United States \nintelligence collection activities are integrated in: (i) collecting against \nenduring and emerging national security intelligence issues; (ii) maximizing \nthe value to the national security; and (iii) ensuring that all collected \ndata is available to the maximum extent practicable for integration, anal-\nysis, and dissemination to those who can act on, add value to, or otherwise \napply it to mission needs.’’\n(c) Subsection 1.5(g) is amended to read:\n‘‘(g)(1) Establish common security and access standards for managing \nand handling intelligence systems, information, and products, with special \nemphasis on facilitating:\n‘‘(A) the fullest and most prompt sharing of information practicable, \nassigning the highest priority to detecting, preventing, preempting, and \ndisrupting terrorist threats against our homeland, our people, our allies, \nand our interests; and\n‘‘(B) the establishment of interface standards for an interoperable informa-\ntion sharing enterprise that facilitates the automated sharing of intelligence \ninformation among agencies within the Intelligence Community.","sections_touched":["Subsection 1","Subsection 1","Subsection 1"],"signing_date":"2004-08-27","source":{"acceptable_as_original":false,"filing_date":null,"grade":"held_text_lead","instrument_id":"EO:13355","page_or_item":"69 FR 53593, PDF pages 1-5","requires_page_check":false,"sha256":"dd9f3555882d2660732d5097285d97db13f57c4b17b801a29bc734ad3c71d474","signing_date":"2004-08-27","text_path":"jobs/clause-drafts/output/texts/cd-job-fr-originals-13355-dd9f355588.txt","text_sha256":"3055ec2869ea20747105a1d149bf5680829d31395ea4933587985d4e2ee7265c","url":"https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/FR-2004-09-01/pdf/04-20051.pdf"},"verb":"amend"},{"actor_id":"EO:13355","char_end":3752,"char_start":1637,"confidence":"medium","how_named":"direct","id":"CHAIN:EO:12333#12","notes":"Change wording lead; chronology does not decide legal effect.","provision_text":"Executive Order 12829, as \namended, is hereby further amended as follows: \n(a) the second paragraph is amended by inserting ‘‘the Intelligence Reform \nand Terrorism Prevention Act of 2004,’’ after ‘‘the National Security Act \nof 1947, as amended,’’; \n(b) Sec. 101(b) is amended to read as follows: ‘‘The National Industrial \nSecurity Program shall provide for the protection of information classified \npursuant to Executive Order 13526 of December 29, 2009, or any predecessor \nor successor order, and the Atomic Energy Act of 1954, as amended (42 \nU.S.C. 2011 et seq.).’’; \n(c) Sec. 102(b) is amended by replacing the first paragraph with: ‘‘In \nconsultation with the National Security Advisor, the Director of the Informa-\ntion Security Oversight Office, in accordance with Executive Order 13526 \nof December 29, 2009, shall be responsible for implementing and monitoring \nthe National Industrial Security Program and shall:’’; \n(d) Sec. 102(c) is amended to read as follows: ‘‘Nothing in this order \nshall be construed to supersede the authority of the Secretary of Energy \nor the Nuclear Regulatory Commission under the Atomic Energy Act of \n1954, as amended (42 U.S.C. 2011 et seq.), or the authority of the Director \nof National Intelligence (or any Intelligence Community element) under the \nIntelligence Reform and Terrorism Prevention Act of 2004, the National \nSecurity Act of 1947, as amended, or Executive Order 12333 of December \n8, 1981, as amended, or the authority of the Secretary of Homeland Security, \nas the Executive Agent for the Classified National Security Information Pro-\ngram established under Executive Order 13549 of August 18, 2010 (Classified \nNational Security Information Program for State, Local, Tribal, and Private \nSector Entities).’’; \n(e) Sec. 201(a) is amended to read as follows: ‘‘The Secretary of Defense, \nin consultation with all affected agencies and with the concurrence of the \nSecretary of Energy, the Nuclear Regulatory Commission, the Director of \nNational Intelligence, and the Secretary of Homeland Security, shall issue \nand maintain a National Industrial Security Program Operating Manual (Man-\nual).","sections_touched":["paragraph i"],"signing_date":"2015-02-13","source":{"acceptable_as_original":false,"filing_date":null,"grade":"held_text_lead","instrument_id":"EO:13691","page_or_item":"80 FR 9349, PDF pages 1-5","requires_page_check":false,"sha256":"61725b64d3753ac07fa1c48e610151280f05e5a75b7426ce2838ad97eb60e9c2","signing_date":"2015-02-13","text_path":"jobs/clause-drafts/output/texts/cd-job-fr-originals-13691-61725b64d3.txt","text_sha256":"c60e620b96ed69b732ecb9f140cff5cf7d9af848c2b7628277c4f04061215157","url":"https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/FR-2015-02-20/pdf/2015-03714.pdf"},"verb":"amend"},{"actor_id":"EO:13691","char_end":9891,"char_start":9064,"confidence":"medium","how_named":"direct","id":"CHAIN:EO:12333#60","notes":"Change wording lead; chronology does not decide legal effect.","provision_text":"(v) Section 3 of Executive Order 13467 is revised to read as follows:\n\n\"Sec. 3. General Provisions. (a) Executive Order 13381 of June 27, 2005, as amended, and Executive Order 10450 of April 27, 1953, as amended, are revoked. By revoking Executive Order 10450 of April 27, 1953, as amended, there is no intent to alter the requirement for an investigation for national security purposes or the \"clearly consistent with the interest of national security\" standard prescribed by that Executive Order for making the determinations referenced in section 2.7(b)(ii). Further, suitability, fitness, credentialing, and national security eligibility regulations, standards and guidance issued by, or interagency agreements entered into by, the Council, the Executive Agents, or any agency pursuant to Executive Order 10450 of\n\nApril 27, 1953, as amended, shall remain valid until superseded. Nothing in this order shall:\n\n\"(i) supersede, impede, or otherwise affect:\n\n\"(A) Executive Order 10577 of November 23, 1954, as amended;\n\n\"(B) Executive Order 12333 of December 4, 1981, as amended;\n\n\"(C) Executive Order 12829 of January 6, 1993, as amended; or\n\n\"(D) Executive Order 13526 of December 29, 2009; or\n\n\"(ii) diminish or otherwise affect the denial and revocation procedures provided to individuals covered by Executive Order 10865 of February 20, 1960, as amended; or\n\n\"(iii) be applied in such a way as to affect any administrative proceeding pending on the date of this order.\n\n\"(b) Executive Order 12968 of August 2, 1995, is amended:\n\n\"(i) by inserting: 'Sec. 3.5. Continuous Evaluation. An individual who has been determined to be eligible for or who currently has access to classified information shall be subject to continuous evaluation as further defined by and under standards (including, but not limited to, the frequency of such evaluation) as determined by the Director of National Intelligence.'; and\n\n\"(ii) by striking 'the Security Policy Board shall make recommendations to the President through the Assistant to the President for National Security Affairs' in section 6.3(a) and inserting in lieu thereof 'the Director of National Intelligence shall serve as the final authority';\n\n\"(iii) by striking 'Security Policy Board' and inserting in lieu thereof 'Security Executive Agent' in each instance;\n\n\"(iv) by striking 'the Board' in section 1.1(j) and inserting in lieu thereof 'the Security Executive Agent'; and\n\n\"(v) by inserting 'or appropriate automated procedures' in section 3.1(b) after 'by appropriately trained adjudicative personnel'.\n\n\"(c) Provisions of Executive Order 12968 of August 2, 1995, as amended, that apply to eligibility for access to classified information shall apply to eligibility to hold any sensitive position regardless of whether that sensitive position requires access to classified information, subject to the Security Executive Agent issuing implementing or clarifying guidance regarding requirements for sensitive positions. Nothing in this order shall supersede, impede, or otherwise affect the remainder of Executive Order 12968 of August 2, 1995, as amended.\n\n\"(d) Nothing in this order shall be construed to impair or otherwise affect the:\n\n\"(i) authority granted by law to a department or agency, or the head thereof; or\n\n\"(ii) functions of the Director of the Office of Management and Budget relating to budgetary, administrative, or legislative proposals.\n\n\"(e) This order shall be implemented consistent with applicable law and subject to the availability of appropriations.\n\n\"(f) Existing delegations of authority made pursuant to Executive Order 13381 of June 27, 2005, as amended, to any agency relating to granting eligibility for access to classified information shall remain in effect, subject to the exercise of authorities pursuant to this order to revise or revoke such delegation.\n\n\"(g) Existing delegations of authority made by the Office of Personnel Management to any agency relating to suitability or fitness shall remain in effect, subject to the exercise of authorities to revise or revoke such delegations.\n\n\"(h) If any provision of this order or the application of such provision is held to be invalid, the remainder of this order shall not be affected.\n\n\"(i) This order is not intended to, and does not, create any right or benefit, substantive or procedural, enforceable at law or in equity by any party against the United States, its departments, agencies, or entities, its officers, employees, or agents, or any other person.\"","sections_touched":["Section 3","section 2","section 6","section 1","section 3"],"signing_date":"2017-01-17","source":{"acceptable_as_original":false,"archival_id":"app:node/218590","filing_date":null,"grade":"mirror_transcription","instrument_id":"EO:13764","location_confidence":"medium","location_verified":false,"page_or_item":"Executive Order 13764—Amending the Civil Service Rules, Executive Order 13488, and Executive Order 13467 To Modernize the Executive Branch-Wide Governance Structure and Processes for Security Clearances, Suitability and Fitness for Employment, and Credentialing, and Related Matters; {"actor_id":"EO:10445","char_end":97704,"char_start":97297,"confidence":"medium","effective_class":"agency_variable","effective_date":null,"effective_wording":[{"char_end":15796,"char_start":15720,"text":"These amendments \nare- effective upon publication in the \nFederal R egister."},{"char_end":17087,"char_start":16970,"text":"Such exceptions from the competitive \nservice shall be effective upon publica­\ntion thereof in the Federal R egister."},{"char_end":19706,"char_start":19618,"text":"Such changes \nshall become effective upon publication \nthereof in the Federal R egister."},{"char_end":25457,"char_start":25442,"text":"Effective date."},{"char_end":25512,"char_start":25459,"text":"This amendment shall \nbecome effective upon issuance."},{"char_end":26614,"char_start":26434,"text":"The foregoing amendment in part \nrelieves restrictions presently imposed \nand must be made effective immediately \nto be of maximum benefit to persons \nsubject to such restrictions."},{"char_end":26868,"char_start":26615,"text":"In part the \namendment imposes further restrictions \nnecessary to prevent the spread of \nvesicular exanthema, a communicable \ndisease of swine, and to this extent it \nmust be made effective immediately to \naccomplish its purpose in the public \ninterest."},{"char_end":27326,"char_start":27164,"text":"=== PDF page 5 of 28 ===\nTuesday , April 14, 1953 FEDERAL REGISTER 2073\nment effective less than 30- days after \npublication hereof in the F ederal  R eg­\nister ."},{"char_end":56725,"char_start":56690,"text":"(1) Effective time and supersedure."},{"char_end":57144,"char_start":56728,"text":"The revised United States Standards for \nGrades of Canned Sweet Cherries (which \nis the fourth issue) contained in this \nsection will become effective thirty days \nafter the date of publication of these \nstandards in the Federal R egister and \nwill thereupon supersede the United \nStates Standards for Grades of Canned \nSweet Cherries which have been in ef­\nfect since May 15, 1940.\n,  (Sec. 205, 60 Stat. 1090, Pub."},{"char_end":58103,"char_start":57862,"text":"After consideration of all relevant \nmatters presented, including the pro­\nposal in the aforesaid notice, the amend­\nment hereinafter set forth is promul­\ngated to become effective 30 dayk follow­\ning publication in the F ederal  R egister ."},{"char_end":62691,"char_start":62537,"text":"It is hereby \nfound and determined that good cause \nexists for making this order amending \nthe order, as amended, effective not later \nthan April 1, 1953."},{"char_end":62887,"char_start":62692,"text":"The regulatory pro­\nvisions of this order amending the order, \nas amended, are such that little or no \npreparation prior to its effective date \nwill be required of handlers regulated \nthereunder."},{"char_end":63338,"char_start":63010,"text":"Therefore, it is imprac­\nticable, unnecessary, and contrary to the \npublic interest to delay the effective date \nof this order amending the order, as \namended, until at least 30 days after its \npublication in the F ederal  R eg ister , and \ngood cause exists, pursuant to section 4\n(c) of the Administrative Procedure Act \n(5 U."},{"char_end":65776,"char_start":64734,"text":"It is \ntherefore ordered, that on and after the \neffective date hereof the handling of milk \nin the Cincinnati, Ohio, marketing area \nshall be in conformity to and in com­\npliance with the terms and conditions of \nthe aforesaid order, as amended, and as \nhereby further amended, and the afore­\nsaid order, as amended, is hereby further \namended as follows:\nAmend § 965.75 (a) to read as follows:\n(a) The market administrator shall \ndeduct an amount not exceeding 6 cents \nper hundredweight (the exact amount \nto be determined by the market admin­\nistrator) from the payments made pur­\nsuant to § 965.73 (b>, with respect to the \nmilk of those producers for whom the \nmarketing services set forth in para­\ngraph (b) of this section are not being\" \nperformed by a cooperative association\nwhich the Secretary determines to be \nqualified under the provisions of the act \nof Congress of February 18, 1922, as \namended, known as the “ Capper-Vol- \nstead Act,” for the purpose of perform­\ning the services set forth in paragraph\n(b) of this section."},{"char_end":66006,"char_start":65865,"text":"C., this 9th \nday of April 1953 to be effective on and \nafter May 1, 1953.\n[ se al ] E zra  T aft  B e n s o n,\nSecretary of Agriculture.\n[F."},{"char_end":66716,"char_start":66515,"text":"Since \na military function of the United States \nis involved, compliance with the notice, \nprocedures, and effective date provisions \nof section 4 of the Administrative Pro­\ncedure Act is not required."},{"char_end":68579,"char_start":68506,"text":"C. 551)\nThis amendment shall become effective on April 15,1953.\n[ se a l!"},{"char_end":71211,"char_start":70046,"text":"These requirements shall be effective \nas to invoices certified after 30 days after \nthe publication of this document in the \nweekly Treasury Decisions-\nSection 8.13 (i), Customs Regulations \nof 1943 (19 CPR 8.13 ( i ) ), as amended, is \nfurther amended by deleting the follow­\ning from the list of merchandise in con­\nnection with which additional informa­\ntion is required;\nTableware, kitchenware, or table or kitchen utensils which  \nare earthenware or crockeryware composed of a nonvitri­\nfied absorbent body not wholly of clay, including white  \ngranite and semiporcelain earthenware, and cream-colored  \nware, terra cotta, and stoneware, and tableware, kitchen­\nware, or table or kitchen utensils not containing 25 per-  \ncentum or more of calcined bone and not hotel or res­\ntaurant ware or utensils, wliich are china, porcelain, or  \nother vitrified wares, composed of a vitrified nonabsorbent  \nbody which when broken shows a vitrified or vitreous, or  \nsemivitrified or semivitreous fracture, or bisque or parian  \nwares; all the foregoing which are painted, colored, tinted,  \nstained, enameled, gilded, printed, ornamented, or deco­\nrated in any manner."},{"char_end":72687,"char_start":72513,"text":"Ds. 50942,51691, and 52011 are here­\nby revoked, effective as to invoices certi­\nfied after 30 days after the publication \nof this document in the weekly Treasury \nDecisions."},{"char_end":77053,"char_start":76708,"text":"If such bond is in order for payment by \nthe paying agent, the owner or coowner, \nupon establishing his identity to the \nsatisfaction of the paying agent and \nupon signing the request for payment \nand adding his home or business address, \nmay receive immediate payment at the \nappropriate redemption value, as pro­\nvided in §§ 315.22 and 315.23."},{"char_end":77963,"char_start":77840,"text":"Compliance with the notice, public \nprocedure, and effective date require­\nments of the Administrative Procedure \nAct (Pub."},{"char_end":79266,"char_start":78844,"text":"Section 500.201 (b) (1) is amended \nto read as follows:\n§ 500.201 Transactions involving des­\nignated foreign countries or their na­\ntionals; effective date. * * *\n(b) (1) All dealings in, including, \nwithout limitation, transfers, withdraw­\nals, or exportations of, any property or \nevidences of indebtedness or evidences of \nownership of property by any person sub­\nject to the jurisdiction of the United \nStates; and\n2."},{"char_end":100205,"char_start":99838,"text":"Provided,  That no award of compensa­\ntion under Public Law 182, 77th Congress, \nto former personnel of the United States \nCoast Guard who served on or after Jan­\nuary 28, 1915, and prior to July 2, 1930, \nshall be effective prior to the date of \nreceipt on or after July 18, 1941, of an \nacceptable application, formal or in­\nformal, as required in claims generally."},{"char_end":101762,"char_start":101685,"text":"O. 11a,  \n426, held text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_10444.txt): it further amends Executive Order 8809 of June 28, 1941 (Good Conduct Medal), as amended by Executive Order 9323 of March 31, 1943, to read as a single restated paragraph, issued under the President's authority as President and Commander in Chief (no authority statute is cited). The restated text establishes the Good Conduct Medal for exemplary behavior, efficiency and fidelity under regulations the Secretary of the Army and the Secretary of the Air Force prescribe, for enlisted men of the Army and Air Force who on or after August 27, 1940 completed three years of active Federal military service, or served one year after December 7, 1941 while the United States is at war, or at the end of service had completed less than three years if any part was after June 27, 1950, with a proviso that no one except persons separated for physical disability incurred in line of duty receives it for under one year. The order has no own-terms end. The three bounded searches were read against their coverage notes. later-events:ofr_catalog has 1 hit, the Office of the Federal Register note that this order amends EO 8809 (with a see-reference to EO 9323); that is the order's own effect on its parent, not a later event against it. current-law:usc has 1 hit: 10 U.S.C. subtitle A, pt. II, ch. 57 note, which prints Ex. Ord. No. 8809 as amended by Ex. Ord. No. 9323, Ex. Ord. No. 10444 (Apr. 10, 1953, 18 F.R. 2069) and Ex. Ord. No. 14085 (section 2, Oct. 3, 2022, 87 F.R. 60541) with no ending statement (release point 119-121, through 2026-10-09). current-law:ecfr has 1 hit that is only a search lead and states no ending. The held text of Executive Order 14085 (87 FR 60541) section 2 amends Executive Order 8809 as amended by 9323 and 10444 by striking men and inserting members and by adding references to the Space Force on or after December 20, 2019 after the August 27, 1940, December 7, 1941 and June 27, 1950 dates; it is recorded as a later event, and under the strike-and-insert ruling the clause continues, amended. The Federal Register issue of April 14, 1953 also prints Army and Air Force regulation notes (32 CFR 578.27 and 878.46, indexed by the packet as an EO 10445 item) whose editorial notes only refer to this order; they are not amendments or an end. The held-corpus search for the number 10444 found no revocation or supersession.\nMember checks: {\"earlier_end_check\":\"No earlier end. The restated paragraph states no date, duration or condition ending the medal. The only later instrument found, Executive Order 14085 section 2 (effective 2022-10-03), amends it and keeps it in force; the U.S. Code note still prints it without an ending statement, and the held-corpus search for the number 10444 found no revocation or supersession.\",\"independent_command_check\":\"The restatement of the parent order is completed by the text it sets out; there is no separate one-time command, deadline or revocation, and nothing in the clause is exhausted by performance. The restated eligibility rule is a standing rule that continues with the medal.\",\"savings_check\":\"No saving clause or transitional provision appears in the order. Eligibility dates in the restated paragraph (August 27, 1940; December 7, 1941; June 27, 1950) are standing eligibility criteria, not time limits on the clause. the whole order (42 FR 58509, signed 1977-11-08): section 1 lets the Administrator of Veterans' Affairs continue monthly educational assistance when an institution closes between terms for not more than 45 days to conserve energy, exercisable once in any 12-month period per institution; section 2 requires the Administrator to advise beneficiaries of the effect on their entitlement. The order has no own-terms end. Held current law: the text of 38 U.S.C. 3680 (release point 119-121 through 2026-10-09) now provides in subsection (a)(2)(A) that the Secretary may continue allowances while institutions are temporarily closed under an established policy based on an Executive order of the President or due to an emergency, capped at 4 weeks in any 12-month period, and its note prints this order. The three bounded searches were read against their coverage notes; current-law:usc hits the note, current-law:ecfr and later-events:ofr_catalog have no hit beyond the order. Authority statute checked in force: clause (A) of former section 1780(a), now 38 U.S.C. 3680(a), is in the held text. The 4-week statutory cap and the statute's use of the Secretary are changes made by statute to the underlying authority, not later presidential instruments, and are disclosed in the clause reason.\nMember checks: {\"earlier_end_check\":\"No earlier end. The order states no duration or date; the 45-day figure limits each closure, not the order. The later-events:ofr_catalog search has no hit and the bounded search of the held corpus for its number finds only the order's own printing and the 1989 codification. The held 38 U.S.C. 3680(a)(2)(A) refers to an established policy based on an Executive order, which supports continuation rather than an end.\",\"independent_command_check\":\"Section 2 (advice to veterans about the effect on entitlement) is a duty dependent on section 1 payments and has no separate end; no other independent command appears in the order.\",\"savings_check\":\"No saving clause. No past payments or entitlements under the order are identified in held sources as surviving independently; state none after bounded search.\",\"scope_check\":\"One clause (sections 1 and 2 read together). Section 1's authority is now exercised under 38 U.S.C. 3680(a)(2)(A), which names the Secretary of Veterans Affairs and caps continued payment at 4 weeks in any 12-month period; the order's 45-day figure therefore operates only within the statutory 4-week limit. That limit is a statutory narrowing, not an ending of the clause.\"}","review_dependency_issues":[],"reviews":[{"file_sha256":"40dbcc0f4db54938d3eb15004cc19b869f5ac9536845f41b85281494a136a7fd","path":"research/excavator/claude-papinian-2026-11-10/y10/packet/complete-v1/receipts/research/excavator/claude-papinian-2026-11-10/y10/packet/reviews/BLIND_REVIEW_A.jsonl","pointer":"line:2","review_kind":"independent_ai_source_review","scope":"whole_case","verdict":"rejected","version_binding":"exact"},{"file_sha256":"ca28e7c6f00f07b14d6b2a3e603c9dbf9a49e155d8c2d49d8d5ba051130bb7f9","path":"research/excavator/claude-papinian-2026-11-10/y10/packet/complete-v1/receipts/research/excavator/claude-papinian-2026-11-10/y10/packet/reviews/BLIND_REVIEW_B.jsonl","pointer":"line:2","review_kind":"independent_ai_source_review","scope":"whole_case","verdict":"upheld","version_binding":"exact"},{"file_sha256":"40dbcc0f4db54938d3eb15004cc19b869f5ac9536845f41b85281494a136a7fd","path":"research/excavator/claude-papinian-2026-11-10/y10/packet/reviews/BLIND_REVIEW_A.jsonl","pointer":"line:2","review_kind":"independent_ai_source_review","scope":"whole_case","verdict":"rejected","version_binding":"exact"},{"file_sha256":"ca28e7c6f00f07b14d6b2a3e603c9dbf9a49e155d8c2d49d8d5ba051130bb7f9","path":"research/excavator/claude-papinian-2026-11-10/y10/packet/reviews/BLIND_REVIEW_B.jsonl","pointer":"line:2","review_kind":"independent_ai_source_review","scope":"whole_case","verdict":"upheld","version_binding":"exact"}],"scopes":[{"aligned_current_scopes":[],"alignment":"scope_or_source_reconciliation_required","different_current_fields":[],"scope_id":"EO:12020#whole"}],"source_pins":[{"held_text":{"expected_sha256":"ebe6d6715948100095d8e26dd7e0a3fafed66d4c664fc6240e8a8f7e140971ef","path":"jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_12020.txt","sha256":"ebe6d6715948100095d8e26dd7e0a3fafed66d4c664fc6240e8a8f7e140971ef","state":"match"},"sha256":"749405498e1b34b8dbdbc32e3a61e2c60e160d533e0d29e651ac4377ef5aec44","text_path":"jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_1202 OF  \nAMERICA\nA PROCLAMATION\nWHEREAS section 4228 of the Revised \nStatutes of the United States, as \namended by the act of July 24,1897, c. 13, \n30 Stat. 214 (U.S.C., title 46, sec. 141), \nprovides, in part, as follows:\nUpon satisfactory proof being given to \nthe President, by the government of any \nforeign nation, that no discriminating duties \nof tonnage or imposts are imposed or levied \nin the ports of such nation upon vessels \nwholly belonging to citizens of the United \nStates, or upon the produce, manufac­\ntures, or merchandise imported in the \nsame from the United States or from any \nforeign country, the President may issue his \nproclamation, declaring that the foreign dis­\ncriminating duties of tonnage and impost \nwithin the United States are suspended and \ndiscontinued, so far as respects the vessels of \nsuch foreign nation, and the produce, manu­\nfactures, or merchandise imported into the \nUnited States from such foreign nation, or \nfrom any other foreign country; the suspen­\nsion to take effect from the time of such \nnotification being given to the President, and \nto continue so long as the reciprocal exemp­\ntion of vessels, belonging to citizens of the \nUnited States, and their cargoes, shall be \ncontinued, and no longer * * * ;\nAND WHEREAS satisfactory proof was \nreceived by me from -the Government \nof Venezuela on October 23, 1940, that \nno discriminating duties of tonnage or \nimposts are imposed or levied in the ports \nof Venezuela upon vessels wholly belong­\ning to citizens of the United States, or \nupon the produce, manufactures, or mer­\nchandise imported in such vessels, from \nthe United States, or from any foreign \ncountry:\nNOW, THEREFORE, I, Franklin D."},{"char_end":26536,"char_start":25820,"text":"Roosevelt, President of the United States \nof America, under and by virtue of the \nauthority vested in me by the above- \nquoted statutory provisions, do hereby \ndeclare and proclaim that the foreign \ndiscriminating duties of tonnage and im­\nposts within the United States are sus­\npended and discontinued so far as re­\nspects the vessels of Venezuela and the \nproduce, manufactures, or merchandise \nimported in said vessels into the United \nStates from Venezuela or from any other \nforeign country; the suspension to take \neffect from October 23, 1940, and to con­\ntinue so long as the reciprocal exemp­\ntion of vessels belonging to citizens of the\nUnited States and their cargoes shall be \ncontinued, and no longer."},{"char_end":34472,"char_start":32810,"text":"Except as provided in section 7 \nof this rule, a person holding a position \nwhen it is placed in the classified (com­\npetitive) service or otherwise is made \nsubject to competitive examination shall, j \nupon recommendation to the Commis­\nsion by the head of the department or \nagency in which he is employed have all \nthe rights which he would have acquired \nif appointed thereto by competitive ex­\namination: Provided:  (a) That he has \nrendered six months of satisfactory ac­\ntive service in the civilian executive \nbranch of the Federal Government im­\nmediately prior to the effective date of \nthe change in status of the position, and \ncontinues to serve in such position for 60 \ndays thereafter; (b) that he shall pass \nsuch appropriate noncompetitive tests of \nfitness as the Commission may prescribe; \nand (c) that he is not disqualified by any \nprovision of section 3 of Civil Service \nRule V or of any other civil service rule \nor by any provision of the Civil Service \nAct or any other statute or executive \norder: Provided further,  that in con­\nferring a classified competitive status \nupon any employee under this or any \nother rule or any statute or executive \norder, the Commission (a) may, in its \ndiscretion, exempt from the physical re­\nquirements established for any position \nany employee who has rendered long and \nfaithful service in a civil capacity for \nthe Government, and (b) may consider a \nperson whose name is carried on the \ncompensation rolls of the Employees’ \nCompensation Commission as having \nrendered satisfactory active service in \nthe position in which he last served for\nthe period which his name is carried on \nsuch rolls."},{"char_end":35568,"char_start":35193,"text":"On the effective date \nof any such order, section 6 of this rule \nshall apply to the positions, officers, and \nemployees of the offices affected, and all \nother provisions of these rules shall be­\ncome applicable to all officers and em­\nployees who so qualify and to all such \npositions thereafter filled in the same \nmanner as they apply to those in offices \nnow classified."},{"char_end":65237,"char_start":64857,"text":"All shipments \nallowable under these regulations shall \nbegin within six months of the effective \ndate of the transfer of the employee un- \nNo. 221-----2\nless an extension is specifically granted \nby the head of the department or estab­\nlishment: Provided,  That in no case \nshall payment be allowable for shipments \nbegun after two years from the effective \ndate of the transfer."},{"char_end":66941,"char_start":66926,"text":"Effective Date."},{"char_end":67049,"char_start":66943,"text":"This or­\nder shall be effective as of October 10, \n1940, and shall be published in the \nFederal R egister."},{"char_end":73856,"char_start":73398,"text":"(a) Whenever the Secretary [of \nAgriculture] finds that the total supply of \ntobacco as of the beginning of the marketing \nyear then current exceeds the reserve supply \nlevel therefor, the Secretary shall proclaim \nthe amount of such total supply, and, begin­\nning on the first day of the marketing year \nnext following and continuing throughout \nsuch year, a national marketing quota shall \nbe in effect for the tobacco marketed during \nsuch marketing year."},{"char_end":121818,"char_start":119225,"text":"It appearing,  That by order entered \nJuly 30, 1936, as amended by order en­\ntered October 31, 1938, the Commission \nentered into an investigation in and con­\ncerning the matter of establishing for \nprivate carriers of property engaged in \ninterstate or foreign commerce, if need \ntherefor is found, reasonable require­\nments to promote safety of operation \nand to that end prescribe qualifications \nand maximum hours of service of em­\nployees and standards of equipment;\nIt further appearing,  That a full in­\nvestigation of the matters and things \ninvolved was had and that the Commis­\nsion, Division 5, on May 1, 1940, made \nand filed a report containing its findings \nof fact and conclusions thereon and on \nthe same date entered an order pre­\nscribing regulations to promote the \nsafety of operation by private carriers of \nproperty engaged in interstate or foreign \ncommerce effective August 1, 1940;\nIt further appearing,  That the Com­\nmission, Division 5, by order of July 19, \n1940, postponed the effective date of said \nregulations to October 1, 1940, and by \norder of September 21, 1940, further \npostponed the effective date to October \n15, 1940;\nIt further appearing,  That the Com­\nmission, Division 5, by order entered \nSeptember 30, 1940,1  vacated and set \naside its order of May 1, 1940, and pre­\nscribed regulations to promote safety of \noperation by private carriers engaged in \ninterstate and foreign commerce which \ndiffered in some respects from the regu­\nlations prescribed by the said order of \nMay 1, 1940;\nIt further appearing,  That the Na­\ntional Retail Dry Goods Association filed \na petition requesting modification of cer­\ntain of the rules so prescribed, and that \non the date hereof the Commission, Di­\nvision 5, has made and filed a report \ngranting said petition in part, which re­\nport and said report of May 1, 1940, \ncontaining its findings of fact and con­\nclusions thereon, are hereby referred to \nand made a part hereof ;\nAnd it further appearing,  That said \npetition having been fully considered by \nthe Commission, and good cause there­\nfor appearing;\nIt is ordered, That effective December \n10,1940, said order of September 30,1940, \nbe, and it is hereby, amended so as to \nadd at the end of Rule 3 (a) of the hours \nof service regulations as it applies to \nprivate carriers of property the fol­\nlowing:\nProvided further, however,  That this \nrule shall not apply with respect to driv­\ners of motor vehicles engaged solely in \nmaking deliveries for retail stores during \nthe period from December 10 to Decem­\nber 25, both inclusive, of each year."},{"char_end":139161,"char_start":138762,"text":"If, during the continuance of the lease­\nhold term herein provided for or any ex­\ntension or renewal thereof, the facilities \nherein leased become unnecessary to the \neffective completion of all the Contrac­\ntor’s contracts within the time scheduled \nfor their completion, this lease shall be \nterminable at the option of either Party \nby the giving of thirty days notice, in \nwriting, to the EO 14085 (signed 2022-10-03; 87 FR 60541; official Federal Register text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_14085.txt, read in full) amends six earlier orders on military decorations and awards (EO 9158 Air Medal, EO 8809 Good Conduct Medal, EO 10694 unit citations, EO 11046 Bronze Star Medal, EO 13830 delegation of authority to approve decorations, EO 11545 Defense Distinguished Service Medal) to cover the Space Force and to use gender-neutral and updated wording, and adds general provisions. Identity: heading, title and date agree with the register row. The dossier inventory fragmented the sections, so I replaced it with eight clauses (inventory override). Own terms: no section has an end date or ending condition. Later instruments: a search of held order texts for the number 14085 finds only the order's own Federal Register copy; the dossier chain lists no event, and the ofr_catalog search records no disposition note naming it. Current law: the U.S. Code (release point 119-121, current through 2026-10-09; laws of 2026-10-10 to 2026-10-14 not reflected) prints each amended order with a status line naming EO 14085: EO 9158 as amended by section 1, EO 8809 by section 2, EO 10694 by section 3, EO 11046 by section 4, EO 13830 by section 5 (notes under 10 U.S.C. subtitle A, pt. II, ch. 57) and EO 11545 by section 6 (note under 10 U.S.C. 1125) (jobs/current-law/output/MENTIONS.csv, USC_EO_NOTES.jsonl); the amended orders are therefore printed as current text with the amendments embodied. One caution is stated plainly: the Code's editorial note under 10 U.S.C. 7276 records that section 4(a) of EO 14085 (substituting Homeland Security for Transportation in paragraph 1 of EO 11046) could not be executed because EO 13286 had already made the identical amendment; section 4(b) to (d) are not affected by that note, and the clause for section 4 is claimed operative on the strength of those paragraphs and the printed amended text, not on 4(a). The order cites no statute as its authority (the Constitution and the laws generally, and the President's office as Commander in Chief); the Code sections the amended orders refer to are not held and I assert nothing about them. The three selected machine searches (current-law:usc, current-law:ecfr, later-events:ofr_catalog) were read with their coverage notes; none carries a coverage warning and none records a revocation or supersession of EO 14085.\nMember checks: {\"earlier_end_check\":\"No clause has an own-terms end. The Code prints each amended order as current, so none was found ended.\",\"savings_check\":\"The order has no savings or transition clause beyond section 7(a), which preserves agency authority and OMB functions. - **ACT:EO:11448>EO:13286**; Sd3145c7b44424f882132e4cb; {"actor_id":"EO:13286","char_end":36505,"char_start":36258,"confidence":"medium","effective_class":"unknown","effective_date":null,"effective_wording":[{"char_end":2501,"char_start":2411,"text":"Executive Order 13260 of March 19, 2002, is hereby revoked effective as of March 31, 2003."},{"char_end":41701,"char_start":40943,"text":"(a)\nin the case of the Department of Defense, the Secretary of Defense has, after consideration of the authority provided under subtitle G of title VIII of the Homeland Security Act of 2002, determined that the exercise of authority under this order is necessary for the timely and effective conduct of United States military or intelligence activities; and\n(b)\nin the case of any other executive department or agency that has authority under this order, (i) the Secretary of Homeland Security has advised whether the use of the authority provided under subtitle G of title VIII of the Homeland Security Act of 2002 would be appropriate, and (ii) the Director of the Office and Management and Budget has approved the exercise of authority under this order.\"."},{"char_end":49577,"char_start":49526,"text":"This order shall become effective on March 1, 2003."}],"exceptions_text":[],"filing_date":null,"id":"ACT:EO:11448>EO:13286","names_target":true,"notes":"Machine lead only; no legal ending or revival asserted. Section 1-101 designates and empowers the Director of the Office of Personnel Management, in consultation with the Director of the Office of Management and Budget, to exercise the President's authority under 5 U.S.C. 5948 to prescribe regulations, criteria and conditions for comparability allowances for certain Federal physicians. Section 1-102 provides that until OPM is established (on or before January 1, 1979) under Reorganization Plan No. 2 of 1978 the Civil Service Commission exercises that authority. The packet's single whole clause covered both, so I corrected the inventory into two clauses with absolute character spans in the held original text: 1-101 operative, 1-102 terminated by its own terms. The held text of EO 12107 (jobs/fr-originals/output/texts/EO_12107.txt, section 1-101) states that the establishment of OPM under Reorganization Plan No. 2 of 1978 is effective January 1, 1979; that is the date on which the until-OPM-is-established condition occurred and the transitional command to the Civil Service Commission ended, by the order's own terms. EO 12107 does not amend EO 12109 and is cited only as the source of the date. Search of held texts for the number EO 12109 finds only the order and 5 CFR part 595 (authority citation); the OFR catalog record has no disposition note; the bounded searches report no machine hit that ends or amends the order. The Office of the Law Revision Counsel U.S. Code release point 119-121 (edition current through 2026-10-09; laws enacted between 2026-10-09 and 2026-10-14 are not reflected in that edition) prints the order as a note and records no ending statement, and the packet holds no source showing a later statute that affects it. 5 U.S.C. 5948 note prints the order's text as current, including section 1-102 as historical text. The held text of 5 U.S.C. 5948 (jobs/theophilus-sources/output/texts/usc-t5-s5948.txt) is in the Code with no sunset provision, and the eCFR search (point-in-time as of 2026-10-14) finds 5 CFR part 595 (physicians' comparability allowances), whose authority citation names E.O. 12109. Section 1-101 is therefore operative as of 2026-10-14.\nMember checks: {\"earlier_end_check\":\"Section 1-101 has no end date, event or condition and no held instrument ends it. Section 1-102 ends by its own terms when OPM was established, which the held text of EO 12107 dates to January 1, 1979; no earlier establishment date appears in held texts (EO 12107 makes the Reorganization Plan's establishment effective on that day).\",\"independent_command_check\":\"The designation of the OPM Director in 1-101 is independent of the Civil Service Commission's transitional exercise in 1-102: 1-102 ended on its own terms on January 1, 1979 while 1-101 continues, so the two are tracked separately.\",\"savings_check\":\"The only ended command is the transitional exercise by the Civil Service Commission, which no longer exists; 5 U.S.C. 5948 and 5 CFR part 595 continue under the 1-101 delegation, so no residual under 1-102 is claimed.\",\"scope_check\":\"Corrected inventory: 1-101 (preamble and designation) and 1-102 (transitional clause) cover the entire held operative text from the authority recital to the signature line, so no command is outside the two clauses.\"}","review_dependency_issues":[],"reviews":[],"scopes":[{"aligned_current_scopes":[],"alignment":"scope_or_source_reconciliation_required","different_current_fields":[],"scope_id":"EO:12109#1-101"},{"aligned_current_scopes":["EO:12109#sec1-102"],"alignment":"exact_quote_and_source","different_current_fields":["state_at_cutoff","first_end","later_events"],"scope_id":"EO:12109#1-102"}],"source_pins":[{"held_text":{"expected_sha256":"9ae30281b4f987b38dd8187581afb84022f046af18cc721c02b4701041940d64","path":"jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_12109.txt","sha256":"9ae30281b4f987b38dd8187581afb84022f046af18cc721c02b4701041940d64","state":"match"},"sha256":"2bbe84367ac61a00fa9305998fc1ffef94854553ab085e5eeed81296a09c918b","text_path":"jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_12109.txt","text_sha256":"9ae30281b4f987b38dd8187581afb84022f046af18cc721c02b4701041940d64"},{"held_text":{"expected_sha256":"9ae30281b4f987b38dd8187581afb84022f046af18cc721c02b4701041940d64","path":"jobs/fr-originals/output/texts/EO_12109.txt","sha256":"9ae30281b4f987b38dd8187581afb84022f046af18cc721c02b4701041940d64","state":"match"},"sha256":"2bbe84367ac61a00fa9305998fc1ffef94854553ab085e5eeed81296a09c918b","text_path":"jobs/fr-originals/output/texts/EO_12109.txt","text_sha256":"9ae30281b4f987b38dd8187581afb84022f046af18cc721c02b4701041940d64"}]}]}

## Valla review leads and component attestations

Review lead only. Every case needs separate applicability, earlier-ending, scope, independent-command, savings and independent whole-case review.

' (a) The President shall award the \nNational Medal of Science (hereinafter referred to as the Medal) \nestablished by the Act, the specifications of which are prescribed by \nExecutive Order No. 10910 of January 17, 1961, as amended, on the \nbasis of recommendations received by him in accordance with the pro­\nvisions of this Order to individuals who in his judgment are deserving \nof special recognition by reason of their outstanding contributions \nto knowledge in the physical, biological, mathematical, or engineering \nsciences."}]},{"affected_orders":["EO:10830"],"availability":"held_not_loaded","kind":"locate_held_provision","reasons":["target provision not located: EO:11562"],"shared_key":"EO:11562","task_id":"TASK:9636d8d7e00b227428de9ac0"},{"affected_orders":["EO:10830"],"availability":"held_not_loaded","kind":"locate_held_provision","reasons":["target provision not located: EO:12345"],"shared_key":"EO:12345","task_id":"TASK:e0cd667bb0d9de6c9ec91d4f"},{"affected_orders":["EO:10830"],"availability":"held_not_loaded","kind":"locate_held_provision","reasons":["target provision not located: EO:13265"],"shared_key":"EO:13265","task_id":"TASK:26452ab2bdbea29b55502352"},{"affected_orders":["EO:10830"],"availability":"held_not_loaded","kind":"locate_held_provision","reasons":["target provision not located: EO:13545"],"shared_key":"EO:13545","task_id":"TASK:4ce46da4f478da11af8b51a2"},{"affected_orders":["EO:10830"],"availability":"held_not_loaded","kind":"locate_held_provision","reasons":["target provision not located: EO:14327"],"shared_key":"EO:14327","task_id":"TASK:9114bdd3fc296cacc64e7097"},{"affected_orders":["EO:12318"],"availability":"citation_or_pointer_only","kind":"operative_current_law","reasons":["No uniquely located attributed legal-text slice is held for this current-law pointer;
